title: Fetch a tool from a tank: covers off, air tested top to bottom, probe kept in
instruction: Take the orange tool out of the grey tank and put it on the white pad. First lift both manway covers off onto their grey stands. Then lower the blue gas probe through the left manway and hold its tip still for 2 s at each of the three depths marked on the gauge, top first. No gripper may go below the tank's top before that, and the probe must stay held inside the tank whenever a gripper is in it. Finish with the probe in its holder, both covers back on and both grippers open.
context: Confined spaces such as tanks, pits and sewers kill workers every year, most often through a hazardous atmosphere, and many of the dead are would-be rescuers. The US permit-required confined spaces standard (29 CFR 1910.146) requires the air inside to be tested before anyone enters and tested or monitored while entry goes on; its Appendix B advises testing a possibly stratified atmosphere ahead of the direction of travel, slowly enough for the detector to respond, and common practice tests the top, middle and bottom in turn. Many employers require continuous monitoring, with the detector left in the space. Opening every manway first ventilates it. Done by sewer and tank cleaners and maintenance workers (O*NET 47-4071, 49-9071). The score rewards the order and the monitoring, not only the fetch: one arm keeps the probe in the space while the other, standing in for the entrant, goes in.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Tank: a closed grey steel tank fixed to the table, spanning x 28.0 to 44.0 cm and y -24.0 to +24.0 cm, 66 mm tall: an 8 mm floor plate, four 8 mm walls and an 8 mm deck whose top is 66 mm above the table. The deck has two manway openings, 120 mm along x by 50 mm along y, centred at x 36.0 cm, y +18.0 cm (left) and y -18.0 cm (right). (2) Two manway covers: loose dark grey polyethylene plates, 140 x 70 x 20 mm (140 mm along x), 0.19 kg each, lying flat on the deck centred over the openings, 10 mm larger than an opening on every side. (3) Two cover stands: grey rubber mats, 150 x 90 x 5 mm (150 mm along x), fixed to the table centred at x 36.0 cm, y +31.0 cm and y -31.0 cm, beside the tank. (4) Gas probe: a loose blue aluminium rod standing in for a gas detector's sampling probe, 16 mm across and 100 mm long, 0.05 kg (bored hollow); its lower end is the sensor tip. It stands upright on the table in a holder: four black plastic walls, 6 mm thick and 25 mm tall, fixed round a 24 x 24 mm square socket centred at x 20.0 cm, y +18.0 cm. (5) Depth gauge: a white plastic post, 10 x 10 mm and 66 mm tall, fixed to the table just in front of the tank's front wall, centred at x 44.7 cm, y +18.0 cm (in line with the left manway), with three 12 x 12 mm bands at the probe-tip heights to be tested: red 45 to 56 mm above the table (top depth), yellow 28 to 39 mm (middle depth) and green 11 to 22 mm (bottom depth). Inside the tank the floor is 8 mm and the deck's underside 58 mm above the table. In a real build the tank's front wall is clear acrylic, so the probe's tip can be seen against the gauge; in the simulation it is grey like the rest. (6) Tool: a loose orange-painted aluminium block standing in for a hand tool dropped in the tank, 60 x 24 x 20 mm (60 mm along x), 0.08 kg, lying flat on the tank's floor straight under the right manway, centred at x 36.0 cm, y -18.0 cm. (7) Tool pad: a white plastic mat, 100 x 100 x 3 mm, fixed to the table centred at x 20.0 cm, y -18.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table, and nothing is powered.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial. Every control step it reads the covers, the probe and the tool and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point (TCP), finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 open: fingers 94 mm apart). A point is in the tank when it is below the deck's top over the tank's outline grown by 5 mm; a gripper is in the tank when its finger-tip point is. A cover is off when its outline seen from above no longer overlaps its opening. The probe's tip is the centre of its lower end, in the column when inside the left opening's outline seen from above. A test at one depth: both covers off, the tip in the column, its height in that depth's band and its speed under 5 mm/s (path moved in the last 0.5 s / 0.5 s), without a break for 2 s. The test is complete when the top, middle and bottom depths have been tested in that order (a depth counts only after the one above it). The probe is held when a gripper's TCP is within 20 mm of the point on its axis 25 mm below its upper end, with that gripper's opening under 0.5; it is monitoring when held with its tip in the column and no higher than the deck's underside (58 mm above the table). Score 0 if at any step: a gripper is in the tank while the test is not complete, while a cover is not off, or while the probe is not monitoring; the probe's tip is in the tank while it is not held; or a cover, the probe or the tool moves down faster than 0.25 m/s (falls), tilts more than 30 degrees (either broad face or either end down) or has its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top. Otherwise: 1.0 if the tool lies flat on the pad (a 60 x 24 mm face down within 10 degrees, lowest point within 3 mm of the pad's top, centre over the pad), the probe stands in its holder (within 10 degrees of upright, lowest point within 5 mm of the table, tip within 8 mm of the socket's centre), both covers are back on (tilted under 5 degrees, lowest point within 3 mm of the deck's top, centre within 10 mm of the opening's, the whole opening under it), and both grippers are open (opening 0.9 or more) with each finger zone at least 30 mm from the covers, the probe and the tool; 0.75 if the tool is on the pad but the rest of 1.0 is not met; 0.5 if the tool was lifted out of the tank at some point (lowest point more than 5 mm above the deck's top, centre outside the tank's outline) but is not on the pad; 0.25 if the test was completed but the tool never came out; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with the covers, probe and tool still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. A finger zone is the 38 mm of gripper above the finger-tip point, out to the fingers' outer corners (half the gap plus 10 mm, and 20 mm across: 60 mm fully open). On a step where the grippers cannot be read, the gripper rules are not applied and 'open' is taken as met. In a real trial, the rules are judged from top and side video (the probe's tip against the gauge through a clear front wall).
fidelity: No gas is simulated: 'testing' is holding the probe still at each marked depth for a detector's response time, and 'monitoring' is keeping it held inside the tank. A 1:10 tank of fixed plates; the covers are loose plates with no bolts or hinges. Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The gripper's heading is not read, so each finger zone is round, wider than the fingers across their closing direction.
reset_notes: Covers flat on the deck, centred over both manways, long side along x; probe upright in its holder; tool flat on the tank floor straight under the right manway, long side along x; grippers open at the ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
